answer: Before payout, each identity must file three reviews of strangers' jobs inside one short tide window, each review graded for specific detail — paraphrase earns zero. Reviews grow into a vine lattice: every job links to its reviewers, and the lattice only pays claims whose reviews strangers rated useful. One operator writing 3n reviews in twenty minutes leaves matching timing and phrasing fingerprints; a whisper network flags the match and merges those clones into one payout share. A fleet of n pays n fees and 3n reviews for one share, so cost climbs faster than n while revenue stays flat.
